content: Diphenhydramine is an antihistamine that is prescribed to alleviate symptoms such as red, irritated, itchy, and watery eyes, sneezing, and a runny nose caused by hay fever, allergies, or the common cold. It can also help relieve itching from insect bites, sunburns, bee stings, poison ivy, poison oak, and minor skin irritations. Additionally, diphenhydramine is used to prevent and treat motion sickness, induce sleep, manage symptoms of Parkinson's disease, and relieve coughing caused by minor throat or airway irritation. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses, so consult your doctor or pharmacist for further information. Diphenhydramine is available in tablet, capsule, and liquid forms for oral administration. It is typically taken three or four times a day. For motion sickness, it should be taken 30 minutes before travel and, if necessary, before meals and at bedtime. For sleep, it is taken at bedtime. Follow the instructions on the package or prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take diphenhydramine exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it or take it more frequently than prescribed. Do not give diphenhydramine to children under 6 years of age unless directed by a doctor. Before taking diphenhydramine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to diphenhydramine or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially other medications for colds, hay fever, or allergies; medications for depression or seizures; muscle relaxants; narcotics (pain medications); sedatives; sleeping pills; tranquilizers; and vitamins. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had asthma, lung disease, glaucoma, ulcers, difficulty urinating (due to an enlarged prostate gland), heart disease, high blood pressure, seizures, or an overactive thyroid gland. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking diphenhydramine, contact your doctor. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking diphenhydramine. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can increase the drowsiness caused by this medication, so avoid consuming alcohol while taking it. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Diphenhydramine may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if any of the following symptoms are severe or persistent: dry mouth, nose, and throat; drowsiness; upset stomach; chest congestion; or headache. If you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: vision problems, difficulty urinating, muscle weakness, excitement (especially in children), or nervousness. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist about the correct disposal method. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Do not share this medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have any questions about refilling your prescription.
